concept_name: Coffee Prince (Cafe, Beverage Bar & Hot Kitchen)

Module 1: Personal Hygiene, Health Clear.Description: Employees perform full 20-second active handwashing with antibacterial soap and potable water at mandatory task transitions, cash handling, and break returns.
ABSOLUTELY ZERO bare-hand contact with Ready-to-Eat (RTE) foods (waffles, pastries, tiramisu, sandwich garnish, culinary ice); tongs, deli paper, or clean gloves used.
Dedicated handwashing sinks in kitchen and barista areas are completely unobstructed, fully functional, and accessible at all times.
Hand sinks are continuously stocked with liquid antibacterial soap, single-use paper towels, and a covered waste bin.
Documented Employee Health Policy active; staff can explain reportable communicable symptoms (diarrhea, vomiting, jaundice, fever with sore throat).
Mandatory 48-hour symptom-free illness exclusion enforced; valid local Health Certificate ID cards (EHS-102) compiled on-site for 100% of staff.
Cuts, wounds, or lesions on hands/wrists covered with waterproof blue detectable bandages PLUS a clean food-grade disposable glove.
Staff wear clean company uniforms and non-slip closed-toe shoes; aprons removed completely before entering restrooms or stepping outside.
Clean hairnets or headwear enclosing hair completely worn by baristas and kitchen crew; front-of-house staff maintain securely tied-back hair.
Fingernails trimmed short, clean, and free of polish, artificial extensions, or acrylic overlays across all food and beverage handlers.
Zero-jewelry policy enforced on lines (plain smooth wedding band only; no watches, bracelets, stone rings, or exposed body piercings).
Personal belongings, cellphones, drinks, and street clothing stored in designated lockers away from prep counters and warewashing sinks.
Eating, drinking from open cups, or vaping/tobacco strictly prohibited in food/beverage prep, dishwashing, and service staging zones.
High-visibility bilingual/pictorial handwashing procedure and glove-changing signage posted directly at all hand sinks and restrooms.
Food safety training records (LOG-TR-01) on-site; staff verified competent in cross-contamination, Big 6 allergen controls, and sanitation SSOPs.

Module 2: Beverage Bar, Steam Wands, Dip.Description: Steam wands wiped downward with dedicated sanitizer cloth and purged for 2 full seconds immediately after EVERY milk steaming cycle.
Steam wand sanitizer cloths kept submerged in dedicated sanitizer bath (Chlorine 50–100 ppm / Quat 200 ppm) and replaced every 2 hours.
Espresso group heads and portafilters backflushed daily at closing using food-grade coffee detergent and rinsed thoroughly.
Blender pitchers rinsed after every drink and sanitized between allergen transitions (e.g., Nutella/Hazelnut to standard) and every 4 hours.
Running water dipper wells maintain continuous potable water flow; if stationary, spoons stored dry and replaced with sanitized tools every 2 hours.
Powder scoops and syrup pumps clean, dry, and stored outside ingredient bins or in clean external brackets (no handles buried in powders).
Syrups, purees, and fruit tea bases stored capped, nozzles cleaned of crust, and labeled with secondary opening expiration dates.
Cooked tapioca pearls held in clean covered containers at ambient temperature with strict 4-hour discard label (TPHC compliant; zero top-filling).
Commercial ice machine interior, deflector curtain, and chute completely free of pink slime (Serratia), mold, biofilm, or mineral scaling.
Ice scoop constructed of food-grade stainless steel/polycarbonate, stored in dedicated clean external holster; zero scoops left inside ice bin.
Multi-stage inline filtration / Reverse Osmosis (RO) system operational; filter cartridge replacement logged per schedule in LOG-UTIL-01.
Monthly accredited laboratory Microbiological Potability Water Analysis Report (PNSDW compliance) current and filed on-site.
Milk pitchers, barista spoons, and shot glasses inverted and air-dried on clean stainless wire racks; zero towel drying.
Bar speed rails, syrup stations, and drip trays cleaned and sanitized every shift; completely free of sticky residues and fruit fly attractants.
Baristas can identify cross-contact risks when preparing drinks with dairy, tree nuts (Hazelnut/Nutella), soy, and wheat ingredients.

Module 3: Cold Chain, 48-Hour Open Dairy.Description: Refrigeration storage units (walk-in, reach-in, under-counter barista coolers) maintain internal product temperatures at <= 41°F (5°C).
The 48-Hour Open Dairy Rule: Opened milk cartons stored immediately in refrigeration at <= 41°F with verified 48-hour discard labels.
Baristas pour only required milk volume per order; ABSOLUTELY ZERO re-steaming, re-heating, or topping-off of leftover steamed milk.
Chilled cream-based pastries (Classic, Strawberry, Biscoff, Matcha KitKat Tiramisu) held continuously in display showcases at <= 41°F (5°C).
Tiramisu mascarpone and whipped fillings protected from temperature abuse during assembly; prep batches limited to 30 minutes at room temp.
All chilled baked goods, whipped cream dispensers, and dessert sauces marked with prep date and calculated expiry date (FIFO/FEFO enforced).
Conspicuous, accurate digital ambient thermometers installed in all barista coolers, kitchen reach-ins, and walk-in chillers.
Internal temperatures of refrigerated TCS foods (milk, cream cheese, cheese sauces, sliced ham, tuna) logged at 4-hour intervals in LOG-TEMP-01.
Commercial freezers maintain foods rock-solid; ambient air maintained at <= 0°F (-18°C) with no excessive frost or defrost breakdown.
Chiller shelves non-corrosive, clean, and not overloaded, maintaining a minimum 2-inch clearance for 360-degree cold air circulation.
Gaskets, door seals, and handles of all refrigeration units clean, flexible, and sealing airtight with zero cold air leaks.
Tuna salad Panini mixes and sliced deli meats held in commercial cold wells or deep ice beds maintaining core temp <= 41°F (5°C).
Whipped cream dispensers (iSi chargers) disassembled, washed, and sanitized daily; nozzles inspected for milk-fat accumulation.
Zero spoiled, sour, or expired dairy/dessert items present in inventory; expired or unlabeled items quarantined immediately in LOG-DEV-01.
Daily cold chain temperature tracking logs reviewed, verified, and signed off daily by the Shift Supervisor or FSCO.

Module 4: Microwave Thawing & Raw Protei.Description: MICROWAVE THAWING PROTOCOL: Frozen proteins (wings, tenders, patties) thawed via microwave transferred IMMEDIATELY to cooking equipment.
ABSOLUTELY ZERO raw poultry or meats observed thawing at ambient room temperature, on prep tables, on floors, or in standing water sinks.
Microwave interior cavity (walls, turntable, ceiling) washed and sanitized after every raw protein thaw cycle to eliminate splatter.
Batch thawing strictly controlled: Only the exact portion count required for immediate batch cooking/frying is retrieved from the freezer.
Alternative refrigerator thawing conducted exclusively on bottom chiller shelves inside dedicated, covered leak-proof drip pans.
Raw chicken wings and meats prepped in a dedicated prep zone strictly physically separated from RTE pastry, bread, and sandwich staging.
Raw protein prep tables and cutting boards washed, rinsed, and sanitized immediately following raw meat manipulation.
Disposable gloves removed and discarded immediately after touching raw poultry; hands washed for 20 seconds before touching other surfaces.
Raw meat marinade containers are food-grade, sealed with airtight lids, and dated with prep and discard timestamps.
Corrugated packaging from raw frozen poultry disposed of directly into lined waste bins; zero contact with clean food contact surfaces.

Module 5: Thermal Lethality, Deep-Frying.Description: POULTRY CCP: Chicken Wings, Chick & Chips chicken, Chicken Ala King, and Cordon Bleu reach internal core temp >= 165°F (74°C) for 15 seconds.
PORK & PROCESSED MEAT CCP: Hungarian Sausages, Spam, Ham, and Bacon cooked to internal core temp >= 155°F (68°C) or >= 145°F (63°C) with 3-min rest.
SHELL EGGS & BREAKFAST: Sunny-side / fried eggs cooked to order reach >= 145°F (63°C); zero pooling of raw unpasteurized shell eggs.
HOT HOLDING CCP: Cooked rice, pasta sauces, and gravies held continuously at >= 140°F (60°C) across service; checked every 2 hours.
RAPID REHEATING CCP: Pre-cooked pasta sauces and cooked rice reheated rapidly to internal core temp >= 165°F (74°C) within 2 hours.
Deep fryer oil quality monitored daily; oil discarded immediately when Total Polar Materials (TPM) exceed 24% or oil exhibits dark smoke/acrid odor.
Digital probe thermometers calibrated weekly (Ice-Point 32°F +- 1°F / 0°C +- 0.5°C) and sanitized with 70% alcohol wipes before/after every probe.
Cooking CCP logs (LOG-COOK-01) record actual verified core temperatures with timestamps and cook initials (no estimated entries).
Panini grill plates cleaned and scraping residues removed between orders (Ham & Cheese, Tuna Melt).
Commercial waffle irons brushed clean, free of carbonized batter crust, and seasoned sanitarily without chemical contamination.
Cooked rice and pasta batches cooled under Two-Stage Cooling (60°C to 21°C in 2h, to <= 4°C in next 4h; <= 6h total) in shallow pans <= 2" deep.
ABSOLUTELY NO double-reheating of previously reheated pasta sauces, chicken gravy, or cooked rice batches.
Plated hot meals dispatched to customer tables within 8-10 minutes of ticket print, preventing ambient thermal decay below 60°C.
Fryer baskets and fry scoops in good repair (no broken wire mesh or loose metal fragments posing physical hazards).
Kitchen line cooks can state the exact minimum internal cooking temperature for poultry (165°F), pork (155°F), and reheated starch.

Module 6: Cross-Contamination & Big 6 Al.Description: Vertical refrigeration hierarchy followed: Top: RTE/Pastries/Breads -> 2nd: Dairy/Beverage Mixes -> 3rd: Cooked Meats/Sauces -> Bottom: Raw Poultry/Meats.
Color-coded cutting board system strictly enforced: RED: Raw Poultry/Meats | GREEN: Fruits/Vegetables/Garnish | WHITE: Dairy/Pastry/Breads.
BIG 6 ALLERGEN SEGREGATION: Hazelnut/Tree Nuts, Dairy, Eggs, Wheat/Gluten, Fish/Tuna, and Soy managed with dedicated utensils.
Dedicated allergen blender jars and measuring scoops used when preparing Nutella and Hazelnut frappes; fully sanitized between transitions.
Baristas and kitchen handlers wash hands and change gloves immediately when switching between allergen-containing and allergen-free orders.
Prominent Allergen Advisory Disclaimer displayed on customer menus and counter signage informing guests of major allergens.
Tuna Melt Panini prep strictly segregated from raw poultry and fresh pastry staging to prevent cross-contact and histamine transfer.
All food, beverage mixers, and dry supplies stored a minimum of 6 inches (15 cm) above the finished floor on clean stainless/epoxy shelving.
Dry goods (creamer powders, pearls, coffee beans, tea leaves, waffle flour) stored in food-grade sealed bins labeled with name and expiry.
FIFO / FEFO inventory rotation evident across all dry storage, reach-in coolers, and pastry display cases.
Supplier lot numbers, manufacturing codes, and secondary prep labels never overwritten, falsified, or altered.
Wiping cloths color-coded and stored submerged in active sanitizer buckets (Chlorine 50–100 ppm / Quat 200 ppm) when not in active use.
Food and beverage tasting conducted strictly using single-use disposable spoons or the Two-Spoon method; zero double-dipping.
Garnishes (banana slices for waffles, burger toppings, tomato/onion) prepped with dedicated sanitized knives and cutting boards.
Customer takeaway packaging (cups, lids, clamshells, straws) stored inverted in clean dispensers protected from airborne splash.

Module 7: 2-Compartment Sink SSOP & Chem.Description: 2-COMPARTMENT SINK PROTOCOL: Pre-scrape -> Sink 1 (Detergent wash) -> Sink 2 (Potable rinse) -> Dedicated Chemical Sanitizer Immersion Tub.
STRUCTURAL COMPENSATION: Mechanical pre-scraping and dry paper towel grease pre-wiping executed before Sink 1 to prevent organic soil loading.
Chemical sanitizer bath (Chlorine 50–100 ppm / Quat 200–400 ppm) maintained in dedicated tub with MINIMUM 2-MINUTE contact dwell time.
Chemical test strips available on-site and utilized every 2 hours to verify sanitizer concentration in the ambient water sanitizing bath.
All washed, rinsed, and sanitized smallwares, utensils, blender jugs, and pans air-dried inverted on clean wire racks; ZERO towel drying.
Cutting boards smooth, non-porous, and free of deep grooves, dark mold stains, or cracks harboring bacteria.
Chemicals, degreasers, descalers, and sanitizers stored in a dedicated locked chemical cabinet strictly segregated from food/packaging.
All secondary chemical spray bottles clearly labeled with chemical name, concentration, and Safety Data Sheet (SDS) hazard pictograms.
Exhaust canopy hood filters, grease drip cups, and ventilation fans clean, degreased regularly, and free of dripping grease hazards.
High-touch surfaces (door handles, POS touchscreens, ice bin lids, fridge doors) sanitized with food-grade disinfectant every 4 hours.
Under-counter cabinets, compressor motor housings, espresso drip trays, and floor corners clean and free of dust and milk crust.
Atmospheric vacuum breakers / backflow preventers installed on sink faucets and water filtration lines to prevent back-siphonage.
Internal grease traps inspected, cleaned weekly, sealed airtight with rubber gaskets, and manifests logged on-site in LOG-GRS-01.
Kitchen floor drains screened, free of standing wastewater, free of organic slime buildup, and emitting zero foul sewer odors.
Master Cleaning Schedule (LOG-CLN-01) visibly posted, assigning specific deep-cleaning duties, frequencies, chemicals, and sign-offs.

Module 8: Integrated Pest Management (IP.Description: Zero evidence of active rodent activity (droppings, gnaw marks, rub marks, urine stains) across dining room, cafe bar, kitchen, and storage.
Zero evidence of German cockroach, housefly, fruit fly (Drosophila), or ant infestation in syrup stations, coffee bar, or kitchen lines.
Active contract with licensed Pest Control Operator (PCO); monthly pest service reports and technician application records filed on-site.
External building perimeter sealed: Front doors, rear exits, service hatches, and windows fit tightly with gaps < 1/4 inch (6 mm).
Screen doors/windows intact (minimum 16 mesh/inch); air curtains installed over main entrance operate properly upon door opening.
Exterior and kitchen access doors kept closed at all times when not in immediate active use.
Waste bins in barista and kitchen stations lined with plastic bags, covered with functional tight lids, and emptied every shift.
External garbage dumpster corral paved, clean, free of organic leachate/spills, and commercial dumpster lids kept tightly closed.
Electronic Insect Light Traps (ILTs) installed away from direct food/beverage prep zones and syrup stations; bulbs replaced annually.
Dry storage shelves positioned at least 6 inches off the floor and 12 inches away from perimeter walls to facilitate pest inspection.
Master Safety Data Sheets (SDS) for 100% of cleaning chemicals and pest control agents archived in an accessible yellow binder on-site.
Legal Chain of Custody & Traceability: Sourcing exclusively from NMIS-accredited dressing plants and FDA-registered suppliers with on-site lot records.
